beats.say: A $5 razor promises a one-time shave. And you keep paying.
Buy the razor alone, no blades included.
Buy the razor with a starter pack of blades.
Buy the razor plus a refill bundle you can actually use.
First year: 51 razors, 168 blades sold. Looks like a mistake.
But it does a job: it creates a blade subscription.
The cheap razor is the hook; it gets you in the door.
In year two Gillette sold 90,884 razors, while blades kept flowing.
Each razor forces a repeat purchase of blades, the real profit driver.
A local gym offers a basic pass for $30 a month.
A class pack for $45 a month, same access plus weekly classes.
An unlimited personal-training plan for $70 a month, which feels like the smart choice because you get everything and more.
Spot the cheap entry that hides a repeat-cost trap. Follow for more.
